correctness.rationale: Reconstructed f_p derivatives and unique inflection at u0=((p-1)/(p+1))^(1/p), endpoint one-sided strict maxima, stationary equality f_p(t)=f_p(N-t) in derivative form. Under t/N=(1-tanh z)/2, the off-center stationary point equation gives N=Qp(z)=2 cosh(z)[sinh((p-1)z/2)/sinh((p+1)z/2)]^(1/p). The explicit monotonicity inequality using G(s)=s coth(s), H(s)=G'(s), and H(s)/s decreasing ensures Qp strictly rises from Nloc to infinity for EVERY real p>1 (no integer restriction). This proves exact count and sign of critical points, including flat strict local minimum at Nloc. Comparing endpoint and center payoffs gives Nglob, the ordering Nloc<Nglob, and the tied maximizers. Expansion log(Qp/Nloc)=z^2/3+O_p(z^4) proves the exponent-independent square-root coefficient. Independent bounded checks 618 comparisons, supporting but not substituting for the analytic argument.

originality.rationale: Hill sigmoidal response and global maximization of sums of sigmoids are established, notably Fazel–Chiang 2005 and Udell–Boyd 2014. The relevant primary section of Fazel–Chiang handles nonconcave rational utilities via semidefinite/sum-of-squares relaxations, not a closed-form theorem for two equal patches and all real p>1. The exact double threshold, complete stationary-point topology and universal square-root onset were not identified as quoted prior statements in actual literature comparisons. Qualified best-of-knowledge due to possibility of elementary previous two-patch derivations.
residual_risks: The scalar two-equal-patch maximization is sufficiently elementary that an earlier unindexed resource-allocation treatment might contain the same two thresholds and root count.
This idealized objective does not yield real-world predator management predictions.

value.rationale: The distinction between local and global optimality in the same motivated response objective, rigorously valid for every real Hill exponent and the universal onset coefficient, identifies a nontrivial allocation trap. Its value is a precise model-theoretic threshold, not an empirical ecological or population dynamics claim.

final_claim: For two identical Hill response functions f_p(u)=u^p/(1+u^p), p>1, under total scaled budget N>0, local equal-split threshold Nloc=2((p-1)/(p+1))^(1/p) is strictly less than global switch Nglob=(2^p-2)^(1/p). Endpoints alone maximize below Nglob, tie with center at Nglob and center alone above; exactly two off-center local minima appear after Nloc with normalized displacement (sqrt3/2)*sqrt(N/Nloc-1)+o(sqrt(...)).
limitations: Only two identical patches, equal predator rates, fixed allocation and instantaneous Hill intake; no stochastic or ecological long-time conclusions.
